---
title: "Serving the hub over a unix socket"
---

`q2 hub` normally listens on a TCP port and speaks WebSocket
(`--host`/`--port`, default `127.0.0.1:3000`). On Linux and macOS it
can instead listen **exclusively on a filesystem unix domain socket**:
no TCP listener is bound at all. The purpose of this mode is the
classic app-server deployment: a same-host reverse proxy (nginx,
Caddy, …) terminates TLS and forwards to the socket, and the hub
itself never touches the network stack — there is no loopback port to
scan, misconfigure, or reach from another process.

UDS mode is always explicit and opt-in; the default never changes.

## Access control

A socket-mode hub is **unauthenticated local-trusted**. Two layers
replace the network checks:

- **Filesystem permissions.** The socket lives in a `0700` directory
  with `0600` permissions, so only processes running as your uid can
  connect — enforced by the kernel even if the application forgot
  every check. (The trusted-proxy shape below relaxes this to a
  group.)
- **An accept-time uid check.** Every connection's uid is verified
  against the hub's own (or an operator-configured allowlist);
  mismatches are dropped and logged.

There is no token validation on the socket, so the proxy in front of
it is the trust boundary: TLS, authentication, and Origin policy all
live there.

## Running a socket-mode hub

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
q2 hub --socket-path                            # the convention path (below)
q2 hub --socket-path /run/user/1000/hub.sock    # an explicit path
```

The bare flag resolves to the convention path:
`<project>/.quarto/hub/hub.sock` in project mode, or
`<data-dir>/hub.sock` with `--data-dir` (standalone mode). If the
resolved path is too long for the platform's socket-path limit (104
bytes on macOS), the hub falls back to a short hashed path under
`$TMPDIR` and records the effective path in a `hub.sock.path` file
next to the conventional location — read that file to learn where the
socket actually went.

Restarting a hub on the same path reclaims a stale socket file left by
a crash; if a *live* hub already answers on the path, startup fails
with "a hub is already running" rather than clobbering it. The socket
file is removed on graceful shutdown.

## Fronting the socket with a TLS proxy

Two flags relax the socket's permissions so a proxy running as a
*different* uid can connect:

- `--socket-group <group>` — the socket's parent directory becomes
  `0750` and the socket `0660`, group-owned by `<group>` (the hub must
  be a member of that group, and fails loudly at startup otherwise).
- `--socket-allow-uid <uid>` (repeatable) — adds `<uid>` to the
  accept-time uid allowlist, so the proxy's workers are accepted. The
  hub logs these connections as "proxied" (its own uid logs as
  "local").

An nginx server block forwarding WebSocket traffic to the socket:

``` {.nginx filename="nginx.conf"}
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name hub.example.com;

    # TLS certificate, edge authentication / Origin policy, …

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://unix:/srv/site-a/.quarto/hub/hub.sock;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
    }
}
```

with nginx\'s worker user in the group named by `--socket-group`, or
its uid listed via `--socket-allow-uid`.

A public proxy with no edge auth means a world-writable hub — the hub
performs no Origin check on the no-auth path, so the proxy must.

## What cannot connect directly

**Browsers and `q2 mcp` cannot dial a unix socket** — hub-client
editing, `q2 preview` sharing, and MCP agents all stay on TCP+WS, which
is why the default never changes. If those clients need the hub, they
reach it through the proxy\'s public TLS address. Share URLs need no
hub-side support: they are built client-side from the browser\'s own
connection URL, so they carry the proxy\'s address automatically.

For debugging, `curl` speaks HTTP over a socket directly:

``` {.bash filename="Terminal"}
curl --unix-socket /srv/site-a/.quarto/hub/hub.sock http://localhost/health
```

## Authentication constraints

Hub-enforced authentication (OIDC) is not available in socket mode:
`--socket-path` combined with `--oidc-client-id` is rejected at
startup. A hub that needs OIDC runs TCP behind its TLS proxy, as
today. `--behind-tls-proxy` is accepted with `--socket-path` but is
inert without OIDC on any transport.
